$comment: Gemma user settings — EXECUTABLE TRUTH (CLAUDE.md hard rule 3). bridge/settings.py derives its DEFAULTS from `settings` here, and teleprompter/SettingsWindow.qml renders its panes from the same file, so a knob is added by editing THIS and nothing else. Never restate a default or a label in code.
$comment_vram: `local_two_model_note` holds the text the Models pane shows when two roles resolve to different models on the SAME local provider. Stated as a fact, never computed: judging whether both fit would need total VRAM, current usage and each model's loaded footprint, and would be wrong often enough to be an annoyance. The failure it warns about is invisible — no error, just a full model reload on every switch between Ask and Dictate, which reads as 'dictation is randomly slow'.
$comment_settings: One entry per knob. `built: false` renders the row dimmed and its control disabled — the setting is decided but its consumer does not exist yet. `pane: null` means no UI row at all (the value is still read by the daemon). `help` is shown only where the consequence cannot be inferred from the label.
$comment_connectors: D38 — the consent gate, one `connector_*` entry per connector at the end of `settings`. `connector` holds the id that schemas/tools.json matches, so a card lists the tools it enables by READING the registry rather than restating them (hard rule 3); `help` is what that connector reaches, shown on the card because switching one on must be consent to something specific rather than to a category. Anything reading personal data is OFF by default (the D23 precedent: a capability stays off until it is asked for) — System is on because the time and the battery are not personal data. Key order is display order. Adding a connector is one entry here plus a `connector` on the tools that belong to it; no UI work.

profile_name.label: Full name
profile_name.$comment: Profile fields persist today; the PERSONA that reads them is M0.5 (spec/00, Track B). Recorded in STATE as owed.

theme.label: Theme
theme.$comment: Dimmed: the app draws one (dark) theme, so choosing light would change nothing. Un-dim when a light palette exists.

language.label: Language
language.$comment: Dimmed: nothing is localised, and STT/TTS are English models (spec/00 fixed platform decisions).

pings.label: Pings
pings.help: Audible tones when Gemma starts listening, completes a task or encounters an error.
pings.$comment: D28. The three designed earcons; a separate channel from spoken TTS.

listen_for_me.label: Listen for me
listen_for_me.help: Always-on microphone. Listens for its wake word, and lets you talk over a spoken reply to cut it short.
listen_for_me.$comment: D23. On = wake word + barge-in; off = the mic opens only on a keypress. Drives the tray's on-air lamp (D29).

tts.label: Read for me
tts.help: Answers are read aloud as well as shown.
tts.$comment: D23/D28. Key name stays `tts` — the file already written to %APPDATA% uses it.

gem_in_island.label: Show Gem in the island
gem_in_island.$comment: D35. Off restores the pre-Gem island exactly — padding, wave width and text column all fall back to their original formulas (asserted in teleprompter/overlay_check.py).

local_server_stop_on_quit.label: Stop the local model server when Gemma quits
local_server_stop_on_quit.help: Gemma calls a local server when running a local model, and closes the server on shutdown.
local_server_stop_on_quit.$comment: Moved to General > Preferences (Thomas, 2026-08-02). Governs ONLY a server Gemma itself started — one already running when Gemma arrived is never stopped, whatever this says (a safety property, not a preference: it may be doing someone else's work). Best-effort on Windows: run.py asks the daemon to stop first (CTRL_BREAK) so this can run, but a hard kill skips it and leaves the server idling until its own keep-alive evicts the model. The Job Object tie (launcher C2, STATE parked) is the complete fix.

models.label: Models
models.$comment: Providers the user has added, keyed by provider id -> {on, model, effort, thinking, ...}. Rendered as cards, not a row. KEY ORDER IS THE DISPLAY ORDER — moveProvider rewrites the dict to reorder.

primary.label: Primary model
primary.$comment: Which enabled provider answers, while more than one is enabled. Stands in for the per-role router (spec/20 reserved, STATE parked).

cleanup_dictation_on.label: Tidy dictation
cleanup_dictation_on.$comment: Paired with `cleanup_dictation` via its `toggledBy` — one row, two values. Read by `orchestrator._dictate`: off skips the transform and pastes the raw transcript.

cleanup_dictation.label: Tidy dictation
cleanup_dictation.$comment: S-06/D15. Resolved by the router (D33) as the `cleanup_dictation` role; unset falls back to CLEANUP_PROVIDER. `modelKey` names the companion setting holding a per-ROLE model override (see there).

cleanup_dictation_model.label: Model
cleanup_dictation_model.$comment: Per-role model override, drawn on the Tidy dictation card and linked from it by `modelKey`. Empty = use whatever model the provider's own card names, which is the pre-existing behaviour. It exists because model hangs off the PROVIDER card, so two roles naming one provider are otherwise forced to share a model — cleanup wants a small fast model while the assistant wants a large one. Narrow by design: it does NOT pre-empt spec/20's Layer 2 (several named instances per provider), which subsumes it.

cleanup_prompts.label: Tidy spoken prompts
cleanup_prompts.$comment: S-06/D15 --clean-prompts. Serves the ASK door, but filed under Dictate with its sibling (Thomas, 2026-07-24) — both are transcript cleanup. Unbuilt.

hotkey_ask.label: Ask
hotkey_ask.$comment: D20. Parsed by bridge/hotkeys.py, which rejects a modifier-less binding.

hotkey_dictate.label: Dictate
hotkey_dictate.$comment: D20. Registered today; its pipeline is Track D.

auto_end.label: Listen for when I stop talking
auto_end.help: Gemma automatically recognises the end of your sentence.
auto_end.$comment: Live today on the VAD silence cut (silence_ms). Semantic endpointing (M1, STATE parked) replaces the MECHANISM later with no UI change — the help text describes the destination, decided 2026-07-24.

silence_ms.label: Silence before a turn ends
silence_ms.$comment: No UI row (decided 2026-07-24): it tunes the interim mechanism behind auto_end and retires when semantic endpointing lands. --silence-ms still overrides.

skip_permissions.label: Dangerously skip permissions
skip_permissions.help: Certain tasks require permission. These can be skipped, but you bear all consequences for any action taken while permissions are skipped.
skip_permissions.$comment: Supersedes D20's narrower `auto_apply`: skips EVERY gate including the Tier-3 confirmation. That converts a spec/50 + CLAUDE.md rule-4 design constant into a preference and needs its own decision record before the executor lands (M1). Placeholder disclaimer.

local_two_model_note.default: Ask and Dictate use different local models and would be limited by memory.
local_two_model_note.label: Two-model VRAM note
local_two_model_note.$comment: `built: false` — the TEXT is settled and lives here so the window can render it without restating a string in QML (hard rule 3), but the condition and the placement are Models-pane work, owed.

connector_system.label: System
connector_system.help: The time and date, the battery, and the title of whichever window is in front.

connector_files.label: Files
connector_files.help: The names and contents of files Windows has already indexed on this PC, so Gemma can tell you where one is. Nothing is opened or read back to you.

connector_email.label: Email
connector_email.help: The sender, date and subject of mail in your desktop Outlook inbox. Message text is searched but never returned, and nothing is opened, replied to or sent.

connector_clipboard.label: Clipboard
connector_clipboard.help: Whatever you last copied, read on request.

connector_web.label: Web
connector_web.help: Pages and search results from the internet.
connector_web.$comment: Dimmed: no tool declares this connector yet — there is no web backend (STATE, Track T).

connector_apps_media.label: Apps & media
connector_apps_media.help: Opening an app, bringing a window to the front, the media keys, and timers.
connector_apps_media.$comment: Dimmed: its four tools are Tier 2, and MAX_TIER holds at 1 until the announce earcon exists. Turning a connector on cannot raise a tier — the two gates are independent.

connector_mcp.label: MCP servers
connector_mcp.help: Tools supplied by an MCP server you connect.
connector_mcp.$comment: D38 holds this slot dimmed deliberately. An MCP tool arrives at RUNTIME carrying no declared tier, so it cannot pass the gate spec/30 rule 1 depends on; admitting one needs its own decision and D-number.

$comment_not_chat: Substrings that mark a live-fetched model id as something other than a chat model, dropped from the picker by bridge/brains/providers.py. A real problem rather than a speculative one: measured 2026-07-24, `GET /models` returns 15 ids for Groq and 129 for OpenAI, including speech-to-text, text-to-speech, embeddings, image generation and safety classifiers — none of which can serve a turn, so offering them as a brain is a trap. Deliberately conservative: matched anywhere in the id, so anything ambiguous is left IN and merely looks odd, rather than hiding a model the user wanted. Add a substring here, never in code.
$comment_providers: The catalogue the Add-a-model flow offers, and the only place a provider's reachability is described (hard rule 3 — bridge/brains/providers.py reads this, never restates it). Per card: `wire` names the protocol that serves it, and there are only two — `anthropic` (B1, bridge/brains/claude.py) and `openai` (B2, bridge/brains/compat.py, one adapter for the other ten). `api` is the base URL for a cloud provider, whose hosts genuinely differ; a local runner declares a user-editable `endpoint` (host:port) instead and B2 composes `http://<endpoint>/v1`, the compat convention Ollama, LM Studio and llama.cpp all share. `env` is the environment variable that stands in when the credential store holds nothing (CI, headless). `models` and `capabilities` are the OFFLINE FALLBACK: the live list comes from the provider's own `GET {api}/models` (Anthropic via its SDK), fetched off a background thread by the settings window, so a card shows what the account can really reach. `adapter` says whether bridge/brains/ can CALL this provider — true everywhere as of D30, because one OpenAI-compatible adapter serves every non-Anthropic entry. Live-verified so far: Anthropic and Groq; the rest share their exact code path but nobody has held a key to them here yet.

google.name: Google
google.$comment: Reached through Gemini's OpenAI-compatibility layer rather than its own genai SDK, so it costs no second wire. Its `thinking` control is not an OpenAI-wire parameter, which is why the capability is declared but B2 does not send it yet.

ollama.name: Ollama
ollama.$comment: `effort` includes `none` because Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint documents that value and treats it as thinking-OFF — one field carrying a switch AND a dial. It is the only way to reach the thinking toggle from here: Ollama's native `think` field and `chat_template_kwargs` are both ignored on /v1 (tested 2026-08-01, v0.32.5). A thinking model left to reason costs ~6.5 s on a dictation cleanup against ~0.45 s without, so `transform` always asks for `none`. Endpoint is 127.0.0.1, never `localhost`: the wasted IPv6 attempt costs ~2 s per connection on Windows.
ollama.$comment_serve: `serve` is the argv Gemma runs to start this server headless when a role resolves here and nothing is listening. Declared per card, never hardcoded in an adapter, for the same reason as `api` and `credential` (D30). It is NOT a Contract T tool and spec/50 rule 1 does not apply: the model never sees it, and this argv is a fixed list from this file — nothing user- or model-composed reaches a shell. Only Ollama declares one; LM Studio and llama.cpp are left to the user to start. The binary is found on PATH, so a missing install is a no-op, not an error.
